title: Neural Network–Based Customer Retention Forecasting in Mobile Wallet Services Using 200k Historical User Profiles
tldr: A modified deep feedforward neural network with leaky ReLU, RMSProp optimization, and batch normalization achieves 89% accuracy and 0.92 AUC on 200k mobile wallet user profiles, outperforming SVM, logistic regression, and standard DNN baselines.
problem_and_motivation: Mobile wallet providers in emerging markets face high customer churn rates that threaten financial sustainability and user trust. Existing retention models rely on traditional statistical methods that fail to capture complex nonlinear behavioral patterns in high-dimensional user data. There is a need for scalable, data-driven approaches that can accurately forecast retention using behavioral, transactional, and demographic features.
approach: Collected 200,000 anonymized mobile wallet user profiles from a Southeast Asian telecommunications operator spanning 2023-2024.
Engineered 23 features across five categories: demographics, engagement, transactions, service usage, and device information.
Developed a modified deep feedforward neural network with leaky ReLU activation, RMSProp optimizer, batch normalization, and 0.5 dropout.
Compared performance against SVM, logistic regression, CNN, RNN, standard DNN, gradient boosting, random forest, and XGBoost baselines.
Evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, AUC-ROC, MAE, MSE, and RMSE metrics.
findings: num: Modified DNN achieved 89% accuracy, outperforming all baseline models.
num: AUC score of 0.92 indicates excellent discriminative ability between retained and churned users.
num: F1 score of 91% demonstrates strong balance between precision and recall.
num: Standard DNN achieved 82% accuracy, showing 7% improvement from architectural modifications.
num: XGBoost achieved 85% accuracy, the best non-neural baseline.
Feature importance analysis revealed transaction frequency and recency as the strongest retention predictors.
Batch normalization and dropout regularization prevented overfitting across training epochs.
The model maintained stable performance across different user segments and service usage patterns.

Figure 2: Training and validation loss curves → demonstrates convergence without overfitting.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper proposes a modified deep feedforward neural network architecture for customer retention prediction in mobile wallet services, demonstrating that architectural modifications including leaky ReLU, RMSProp, batch normalization, and dropout yield measurable improvements over standard baselines. The study provides empirical evidence from 200k user profiles showing that behavioral, transactional, and demographic features can be effectively integrated for retention forecasting. The feature importance analysis identifies transaction frequency and recency as primary predictors, offering actionable insights for retention strategy design. The comparative evaluation against nine baseline models establishes a performance benchmark for mobile financial service retention prediction.
directly_justifies: Modified DNN achieved 89% accuracy, outperforming all baseline models including XGBoost at 85%.
AUC score of 0.92 indicates excellent discriminative ability between retained and churned users.
Transaction frequency and recency emerged as the strongest predictors of customer retention.
Batch normalization and dropout regularization prevented overfitting across training epochs.
limits: The model was trained and evaluated on data from a single Southeast Asian operator, limiting cross-market generalizability.
The static feature set does not account for temporal drift in user behavior over extended periods.
No fairness or bias analysis was conducted across demographic subgroups.
The model lacks interpretability, making it difficult to explain individual predictions to stakeholders.
